title: Two problems, solved end to end

problems.label: Problem A · engineering + AI
problems.title: Turning a flood of numbers into decisions
problems.who: For the people who run the business: finance, operations and store managers.
bullets: Every system sends its numbers every minute, and we check them before anyone sees them.
Each number is compared to what's normal for that store, day and hour.
AI writes a one-page morning report and fast alerts, and never makes up a number.
problems.cta: Follow a file to a decision

problems.label: Problem B · frontend + product + AI
problems.title: Personal, and still instant
problems.who: For every shopper, on the site and in the app.
bullets: It learns from what you view, save and buy, and which store is near you.
It suggests similar items you can actually get: in stock, in your size, nearby.
Pages stay fast while AI works, and a virtual fitting room opens once you pick a size.

banner: Build what makes you different. Buy what everyone needs. Every choice gives something up; the skill is choosing what to give up.

items.text: < 2 min from a problem to an alert
0 numbers written by the AI itself

report.headline: Revenue in São Paulo stores is 12% below a normal Monday since 14:00
report.cause: Likely cause: card terminals failing at 3 stores since 13:52.
report.suggestion: Suggested: switch them to the backup payment provider.

honesty.title: Numbers come first
honesty.plain: Every number is calculated from the stored data before the AI sees anything.
honesty.engineering: SQL over the analytics store; results passed to the model as a typed payload.

honesty.title: The AI only writes the sentence
honesty.plain: It receives the finished numbers and turns them into one clear sentence. It can't add new ones.
honesty.engineering: Prompt carries only the payload of totals; no personal data; temperature 0.

honesty.title: A checker reads it before you do
honesty.plain: Every number in the text is matched against the source. One mismatch and the report doesn't go out.
honesty.engineering: Extract numbers from the text, compare with the payload within tolerance, fail closed and alert a person.

segments.label: Next page loads before you scroll

techniques.title: Page by page, not all at once
techniques.plain: 24 items and a bookmark to the next page.
techniques.engineering: Cursor pagination, a stable sort key and no deep offset scans.

techniques.title: Draw only what's on screen
techniques.plain: About 20 rows kept in the page and recycled as you scroll.
techniques.engineering: List virtualization with overscan; heights reserved so nothing jumps.

techniques.title: AI never blocks the page
techniques.plain: Suggestions fill a reserved space; if the AI is slow, show bestsellers in your size.
techniques.engineering: Streamed server rendering, fixed-height slots (no layout shift), 800 ms timeout with a cached fallback.

techniques.title: Save the common answers
techniques.plain: The first page is prepared in advance and served from a nearby cache.
techniques.engineering: Edge-cached first page, idle-time prefetch of the next cursor, and stale-while-revalidate.

points: Problem A is what a performance-intelligence platform does every day across creators and platforms.
Problem B is how fans and brands would experience it.
The build-vs-buy map is how a founding engineer spends a small team's time.

steps.title: Two problems
steps.caption: Two problems, each solved end to end, in plain language first.
steps.presenterNote: I want to show you two problems I'd expect to solve in the first months, end to end. Everything is in plain language, and the engineering is one key away.

steps.title: Problem A
steps.caption: Turning a flood of numbers into decisions.
steps.presenterNote: The first is about numbers: turning a flood of results files into one clear decision every morning.

steps.title: Problem B
steps.caption: Personal, and still instant.
steps.presenterNote: The second is about people: making the product feel personal without ever making it slow.

steps.title: Build or buy
steps.caption: Build what makes you different. Buy what everyone needs.
steps.presenterNote: And across both, the real founding-engineer skill: deciding what to build, what to buy, and what we give up.

What people see, and how we keep the AI honest

steps.title: The morning report
steps.caption: One sentence, a chart with the normal range shaded, and the moment things changed.
steps.presenterNote: This is what a manager actually sees: one sentence, a chart with the normal range shaded, and the moment things changed.

steps.title: Likely cause, suggested fix
steps.caption: The AI proposes a cause and a fix; a person approves it.
steps.presenterNote: Then the likely cause and a suggested fix, which a person approves. The AI proposes and people decide.

steps.title: How we keep the AI honest
steps.caption: Numbers first, the AI writes only the sentence, and a checker reads it before you do.
steps.presenterNote: This is how we keep it honest: numbers first, the AI writes only the sentence, and a checker reads it before you do.

screens.title: Problem A: what we build, what we buy

steps.title: What we build
steps.caption: What defines the business stays ours: the checks, the meaning of revenue and profit, and what counts as unusual.
steps.presenterNote: Here's what we build ourselves: the things that define the business, like what revenue means and how we spot unusual numbers.

steps.title: What we buy
steps.caption: Heavy machinery everyone needs is bought: the database, the AI model and the dashboards.
steps.presenterNote: And here's what we buy: the database, the AI model and the dashboards, because running those well is someone else's full-time job.

steps.title: What we give up
steps.caption: Every choice has a cost, in amber. We choose which cost to accept.
steps.presenterNote: Every line has a cost in amber. Buying means a bill and some dependence, and building means we own every fix.

steps.title: The race
steps.caption: The same page, built two ways, on the same five-second clock.
steps.presenterNote: Here's the trade-off drawn honestly: the same page built the simple way and the way I'd build it, on the same five-second clock.

steps.title: Useful at 0.6 s
steps.caption: 4.8 seconds of blank screen, or something useful at 0.6 seconds.
steps.presenterNote: The simple way shows nothing for almost five seconds. Ours is useful at 0.6 seconds, and the AI picks slide in when they're ready.

steps.title: Four techniques
steps.caption: Page by page, only what's on screen, AI never blocks, common answers prepared.
steps.presenterNote: Four techniques do it: load page by page, draw only what's on screen, never let AI block the page, and prepare the common answers in advance.

steps.title: Try it live
steps.caption: 2,000 products in your browser, with a simulated AI slot and a live readout.
steps.presenterNote: And this isn't a slide: 2,000 products are loading page by page in your browser, with a simulated AI slot that gives up after 800 milliseconds.

screens.title: Problem B: what we build, what we buy

steps.title: What we build
steps.caption: Ours: how suggestions are ranked and how fast every page feels.
steps.presenterNote: We build the two things a shopper actually feels: which suggestions come first, and how fast every page is.

steps.title: What we buy
steps.caption: Bought or open source: product understanding, the fitting room, tracking and images.
steps.presenterNote: Everything that's hard but generic we buy or take as open source: understanding products, the fitting room, tracking and images.

steps.title: What we give up
steps.caption: Costs per product, per try-on and per month, each one limited on purpose.
steps.presenterNote: Each choice has a price, and each price has a limit we chose: the fitting room only opens after a size is picked.

steps.title: The map
steps.caption: Across: how much it makes us different. Up: how hard it is to do well.
steps.presenterNote: This is the one picture I use to spend a small team's time: across, how much something makes us different, and up, how hard it is to do well.

steps.title: Problem A
steps.caption: What defines the business is built now; the heavy machinery is bought.
steps.presenterNote: Problem A lands in build now for what defines the business, and buy for the heavy machinery.

steps.title: Problem B
steps.caption: Suggestion ranking is built later: a ready tool first, ours once there is data.
steps.presenterNote: Problem B puts suggestion ranking in build later: start with a ready tool while there's no data, then replace it.

steps.title: How I decide
steps.caption: Four questions decide every dot.
steps.presenterNote: Four questions decide every dot: is it why customers choose us, is it hard and generic, can we swap it later, and what does it cost at ten times the volume?
